# Hardening notes — hogee run-10

Hunter hardening notes kept in ledger bookkeeping (not findings; no verdicts). Grouped by hunter.

**h-cfo**

- final-1 and final-2 share the FINAL key set: keySetForDeployment (apps/worker/src/config/keys.ts:36-39) maps every final-* deployment to FINAL, and the keys.ts:5 comment still describes only loop/final separation. They run on the same chain with separate DB nonce allocators, and only the runbook stops the two running at once. Reconcile does detect a collision (an agent-key halt plus safety pause, alerts for the other keys). Per-deployment key-set names would restore separation.
- Worker preflight (apps/worker/src/runtime/app.ts:97-137) never checks Treasury.registry() against the manifest's PlanRegistry. Because final-1 and final-2 share the lender key, the PlanRegistry.lender() check no longer catches a DEPLOYMENT_FILE that pairs one deployment's Treasury with the other's registry. Downstream checks fail closed, and VerifyFinal.s.sol:123 checks the link only at deploy time. Add a readContract of Treasury.registry() to checkLinks.
- API snapshot reads are pinned by block number, not hash (packages/api/src/services/snapshot.ts:89), while the CFO report cache is keyed by the head hash (packages/api/src/services/cfo.ts:374). The new 1 s block-lag retry re-reads the same number, possibly from another backend, which slightly widens an existing window in which a head reorg could mix two blocks in one snapshot. Consider EIP-1898 blockHash pinning, or checking that getBlock(N).hash equals the head hash. This is display-level only; the contracts bind the money.
- GET /api/balances and /api/stats/autonomy have no server-side limiter or cache (docs/decisions/fix-cfo-load.md:38-41), and each is a full chain snapshot of about 15 + 3 per line RPC reads, now retried at most once per read on lag. This predates the range. It matters only for a hosted live deployment where an unauthenticated GET flood could spend an RPC quota shared with the worker.
- MIN_FREE_CONNECTIONS = 3 (apps/worker/src/runtime/job-locks.ts:24) understates cfo-guard's peak parallelism (about 5 concurrent pool queries in readGuardInputs, apps/worker/src/jobs/cfo-guard-inputs.ts:75-80,175-179). Extra queries queue briefly with 4 connections free, so there is no deadlock, but the budget test does not model it.

**h-chat**

- packages/api-mock/src/journey/index.ts cannedTemplate (canned default and MY scenarios): re-check mockSessionFull(st, sessionId) inside the oneAtATime callback before pushing, as say() does. Today the only check is in streamChatTurn before queueing (chat.ts:29), so a burst of concurrent quick or CFO template turns can push one session past CHAT_SESSION_MAX_MESSAGES by 2 per in-flight request. Regression case: N parallel 'is my money safe?' posts at 598 messages leave at most 600 stored.
- packages/core/src/journey/quick.ts GUARD is /[0-9%]/, ASCII only. Full-width digits and '％' (which foldForAmounts NFKC-folds and grounding then parses) and other-script digits pass, so a deal report or budget typed with them ('who is the supplier? went with #２, ３０％ deposit') gets a quick template instead of reaching report_terms or the planner. This is a same-principal misroute; the text stays in history. Run the guard over NFKC-folded text with \p{Nd} and ％.
- packages/agent/src/planner/grounding.ts binds a figure, not its role. Any non-negated facility-currency amount in the latest money-talk user turn grounds: savings, a routed-stage deal total read back on a later replan, a Chinese negation ('不是 S$50,000'; NEGATED_BEFORE is English/Malay only), and an amount whose foreign marker is separated by '/' ('US$ / 10,000 SGD', where MARKER_BEFORE's gap set is [ :=(]). No attacker content reaches the planner context, and every draft still needs the founder's PlanApproval passkey signature under the facility cap, so this is defence in depth only.
- packages/api/src/journey/text.ts quickTurn calls quickReply without QuickHints, so in the live API a founder with a pending (not yet approved) passkey asking 'what now?' at INTAKE is told to set up a passkey (founderKeyActive is false). This is wording only and the mock passes hints; pass passkeySetUp from the founder-key facts.

**h-demo**

- apps/web/scripts/dev-mock.mjs:24: refuse to start when MOCK_API is set to anything but "1" (REPLAY aside), instead of keeping an inherited MOCK_API=0. Print the mode route.ts will actually resolve rather than the fixed 'Mock mode' and 'Sample business (lived)' (:43,45). Consider building the child environment from an allowlist, as dev:live's baseEnv does, and add a dev-mock.test.mjs case for MOCK_API=0. As it stands, the live API runs with DEMO_MODE=1 forced and the operator's full environment, and apps/mcp (whose README points it at dev:mock) reaches live instead of the mock.
- packages/api-mock/src/demo-data.ts:36-37 buffers the whole body with c.req.text() before applying the 256-byte limit. Check Content-Length and cap the stream before reading. The same pattern exists in http.ts readBody for every mock route.
- Each accepted POST /api/demo/sample-business re-reads the fixtures and replays the whole lived story (store.ts:186-188, scenario-lived/build.ts playStory), and an abandoned in-flight build keeps running on a detached store. Serialise or rate-limit rebuilds; this matters only once the operator gate is decided.
- apps/web/next.config.ts sets no allowedDevOrigins, and no Host check covers /_next/* or the dev overlay endpoints (proxy.ts matches pages only and sets the CSP). Set an explicit non-empty allowedDevOrigins so Next's dev cross-origin check runs in block mode if 16.4.0 still defaults to warn. In next dev, also consider a Host allow-list for non-/api paths, because DNS-rebound same-origin GETs carry no Origin header.
- pnpm-workspace.yaml: set minimumReleaseAge explicitly, so the release-age gate that docs/VERSIONS.md:10 relies on does not depend on a pnpm default.

**h-evidence**

- Bundle-row tx hashes link to the pinned explorer whether or not the browser check passed (evidence-table.tsx:64 in replay and live; e2e/smoke/evidence.spec.ts:226 expects a failing pack's row to link). A tampered pack can therefore send a judge to an unrelated real Sepolia transaction. The explorer.ts:3-5 comment claims it cannot, which is true only for explorerUrl. Gate row links on result.ok, or on the row chain equalling the verified anchor chain.
- Proof figures and the rows table come from the API's parsed JSON (getEvidenceRun rows, evidence-view.tsx:121, :136), not from the evidence.json bytes the browser verified. They agree only because the mock and live server re-read the same disk file. Derive counts and rows from the verified files to bind them.
- useVerify caches the verdict under ['verifyBundle', runId, files.length] with infinite staleTime (verify-panel.tsx:36), so a pack changed in place with the same file count keeps its earlier verdict until the cache is dropped. Include a content hash, such as hashes.json's keccak, in the key.
- The mock re-reads and re-parses manifest.json, evidence.json and contracts.json (up to 4 MiB each) synchronously on every getEvidenceFile request (evidence.ts:341-345, :371-372). A page verify fans out to one such parse per bundle file, up to 500. Memoize the parsed index by (dir, mtime, size).
- The verifier accepts manifest.deployments entries beyond contracts.json's deployment (tools/verify-evidence/src/audit.ts:87-88, unchanged in this range). Making it require exactly that one deployment would close the root of the recordedLabel candidate for every consumer, including the pre-existing Versions links of forged entries.

**h-facts**

- packages/core/src/journey/actions.ts:160-164 (new in range): any `signed` hint whose MilestoneRelease refId equals the journey's orderId gets 'Signed. The balance is paid once it's saved.' This fires at any stage, including COOLING and a bindFailed order, and with no server fact that a release was signed. The PlanApproval and SupplierApproval branches do check server state. The impact is limited to the hinting session's own text. Suggested fix: gate the branch on hasOrder(state.stage), on bindFailed !== true, and on a server fact such as a RELEASE_MILESTONE payment row for that order. Otherwise fall back to TEXT.signatureNoted.
- Live and mock differ on the supplier list. Live journey facts read the facility-wide newest shortlists row (packages/api/src/journey/facts.ts:70-79); the mock reads the session's own latest list (packages/api-mock/src/journey/facts.ts:59-60). A search started in another live chat session can move this session back from PICKED to CANDIDATES. It cannot change terms, orders or sign cards (same founder principal), so this is a parity and UX note, not a boundary.
- The lifecycle exit for an unbound order (syncFailedBinds) runs only inside relay and agent-actions, which skip when the lock is busy, while reconcile now waits for it. Running syncFailedBinds from reconcile as well would let the CANCELLED exit benefit from the 20 s wait.

**h-mock-a**

- Catalog SupplierApproval funding has no room check and no outflow bound: signing.ts:418-427 applySupplierApproval and supplier-order.ts:45-55 newSchedule. Live planOrder calls requireCatalogRoom (supplier-approval.ts:112), and the range applies outflowRefusal to web funding, spends and autonomy, but not here. In lived the two sample web orders already hold part of the SUPPLIER pocket, and a catalog order for the rank-one supplier commits goods of min(landed, 80% of allocated) and funds sample plus deposit at once. Run-9 rejected this class as the founder's own simulated budget; still worth applying outflowRefusal and a mockLimits room check.
- supplier-order.ts:60-65 still falls back to the rank-one catalog candidate for an escrow order id that no shortlisted supplier owns, and re-approves existing orders. Refuse existing orders and order-w ids, as live planOrder does (supplier-approval.ts:92-99). Lived now seeds two order-w ids by default.
- Web deposit funding checks only the released bound (orders.ts:300, releasedOnly at spend-policy.ts:46-49). In fresh, a web deposit therefore settles, and its trace says 'settlement confirmed on-chain', while fundedMinor is 0 and the chain's fundMilestone would revert. Apply the funded bound, or label the shortcut to the user.
- Lived builder traces dated in the sample history have no Sample label: recordInspection's 'Founder uploaded inspection evidence' (build.ts:257, supplier-order.ts:83), 'Founder confirmed terms' (build.ts:283, orders.ts:250), 'Loan officer funded the facility' (build.ts:224), and the ADD_PAYEE request and 'Loan officer approved' (build.ts:231, 247). The adjacent SIGNATURE traces do say 'Made up for the demo'. Pass a sample marker into these traces.
- milestoneRelease uses Date.now() for its PayeeCooling check (signing.ts:173), and submitSignature defaults to Date.now() (signing.ts:340), while buildSignatureRequest and the rest of the mock use mockNow(). A future story step could pass a release during cooling at build time. Use mockNow() throughout.
- applyPlanApproval's re-sign branch (signing.ts:406-411) writes the tx of any same-version draft onto the committed plan without comparing planHash. In fresh and lived, the SG example alias draft (draft-mei-001) sits beside plan-draft.json. Refuse unless planHash matches.
- The LoosenRequest panel row hard-codes 'demo: 120 s' (signing.ts:250), but queueLoosen uses env.timelockSeconds (DEMO_TIMELOCK_SECONDS). Render the configured value.
- Mock terms confirm skips the holder/seller sanctions screen that live runs (supplier-terms.ts screenTermsNames). The shortcut is documented only in the orders.ts:6 header. The seller is screened at search and the holder must match it, but nothing labels this for the user.

**h-mock-b**

- packages/api-mock/src/spend-policy.ts:19-25 payeeBound (new in range) treats any EXECUTED ADD_PAYEE as binding forever and at once. Treasury._requirePayeeReady (contracts/src/TreasuryState.sol:272-276) also requires _listedVersion == _planVersion, so a re-commit drops the payee, and now >= coolingUntil, a fresh cooling period per add (TreasuryLoosenRules.sol:117-127). Mock createException also skips core addPayeeRules (escrow-only line, platform payee, expired line). No non-operator gain: only the lived builder and the exampleInvoice payee can be paid that way, both after founder and officer approval. Suggested fix: stamp the plan version and an executedAt plus cooling on ADD_PAYEE execution, and check both in payeeBound. Regression cases: after a v2 commit the payee is PayeeNotBound; inside cooling the refusal is PayeeCooling.
- packages/api-mock/src/features/orders.ts:300 calls outflowRefusal(st, amount, true), which skips the funded bound. fundWebMilestones also never checks the SUPPLIER pocket's allocated - spent - escrowed, while Treasury.escrowFund enforces both (contracts/src/TreasuryModuleHooks.sol:38-41). In the fresh scenario the mock can settle a web deposit before the officer funds anything. The gap is documented in spend-policy.ts:42-45, and there is no attacker gain. Suggested fix: drop releasedOnly once fresh-journey tests fund first, and add the pocket bound.
- packages/api-mock/src/exceptions.ts:204-208 with effects.ts:42-45: the mock's officer RELEASE_STAGE approval has no stage-0, already-released, plan-total or gate check. Live has all four (exception-create.ts:35-41; routes/exceptions.ts:108-110; relay-calls.ts:225-227). Since this range the new outflow bound reads releasedMinor, so an officer who approves a duplicate RELEASE_STAGE raises the mock's released bound past the plan total. This needs the officer persona. Suggested fix: refuse an unknown, first or released stage and a pending duplicate at create and approve, and mark the stage released.
- packages/api-mock/src/handlers-ops.ts:90-96: mock proposeSpend (MCP propose_spend) accepts any unused pacingSlot integer, so slots can be skipped or many paid in one day. The chain requires slot == seq + 1 (TreasuryState.sol _requireInvoice), and live allows one slot per line per chain day. The window, pocket and outflow caps still bound it. Pre-existing.
- packages/core/src/policy/loosen.ts:93-98 withdrawRules accepts any isPlatformPayee destination. Every live caller is safe only because loosenIn applies reserveTaxPayee first. Defence in depth: give PolicyContext the facility's tax payee id and require it in core.
- packages/api-mock/src/scenario-lived/build.ts:12-14 claims every proposal reads 'Sample: ...'. Builder-made web-order FUND_MILESTONE and RELEASE_MILESTONE proposals (features/orders.ts:303,306-318; signing.ts:440) and traces from recordInspection, confirmOrderTerms, officerApprove and fundFacilityWith carry no Sample label in the lived store. This is wording only: the mode badge and welcome text mark the scenario as sample.
- packages/api-mock/src/signing.ts:250: the LoosenRequest signing rows hard-code 'demo: 120 s' while DEMO_TIMELOCK_SECONDS is any positive integer (env.ts:101,112). The display can disagree with the real waiting time; the signed struct is unaffected.

**h-web-a**

- rule-list SourceUrl links any https host. TIER_LABEL ('Official government page') shows the pack's own evidence tier and is not checked against the link host. Writers today are operator-curated packs, fixtures and REPLAY snapshots only. A per-pack allow-list of official source hosts would make the label and the link agree.
- REPLAY snapshot plan-current.json is zod-validated, but nothing binds its manifest (rule ids, sourceRef, verifiedOn) to its planHash. approvalStepOf and packDepth trust those fields. Checking planHash(manifest) === planHash at seed load would close this for operator-supplied bundles.
- Some money readers show the last figures with no stale note while a CFO or balances refresh is failing or held: stage-gate-card useSales, OfficerStats, wallet-rail and cfo-panels NextRelease. Live /api/cfo uses one shared LOCAL_CLIENT bucket under Next, so another browser can keep it at 429. Use queryView/RefreshNote there too.
- SECTION_JUMP_EVENT (section-nav.tsx onRequest) accepts any regex-valid element id, not just the page's listed sections, so same-origin code can focus and scroll any element by id. Restricting it to sectionsFor(pathname), as the hash path already does, keeps the jump inside its documented scope.
- raisePrefill accepts up to 30-digit minor amounts from the URL. The form shows the amount and needs a typed reason, both signatures, the officer and the timelock, but capping `to` at a plausible maximum (e.g. the facility cap) would remove an outsized prefill.

**h-web-b**

- apps/web/components/chat/cards/sign-host.tsx:124 passes the opener's title into the sign sheet's DialogTitle. For a chat SupplierApproval that title is orderSheetTitle(candidate.displayName) (apps/web/components/chat/cards/terms-card.tsx:83, order-copy.ts:239): the third-party web listing name, not bound to the signed message. Meanwhile apps/web/components/sign/sign-dialog.tsx:214 says the passkey 'signs exactly what's shown here'. The signed holder appears in the summary and the unverified line, so nothing unseen is signed. Use KIND_TITLE, or build the title from check.webOrder.holderName.
- apps/web/components/sign/sign-dialog.tsx:113-116 memoizes checkSignatureRequest without the clock, so the expiry test never re-runs while the sheet is open, and Sign stays enabled past expiresAt until the API or contract refuses. Add useNow() to the memo dependencies.
- apps/web/components/sign/seal-time.ts:30,36: zonedDate and zonedDateTime throw RangeError for a finite but out-of-range unix value (e.g. a uint64 expiry or agentExpiry). That crashes the sheet's render instead of showing a 'can't show this' reason. It fails closed, but structProblem should reject expiries it cannot render.
- apps/web/components/chat/next-step.tsx:174: the tint selector for a non-plan signature matches any [data-testid=card-terms] [data-testid=terms-submit], not the waiting refId. While a newer deal form is on screen, the tinted bar opens the older waiting order's sheet. Bind the selector to the refId.
- apps/web/lib/api/use-session.ts:12-21: after a successful switch, the officerToken stays in the useSetPersona mutation variables in memory. Calling setPersona.reset() in onSuccess drops it.
- apps/web/components/sign/passkey-setup-card.tsx:178 and apps/web/components/sign/enrolment-form.tsx:71 name the code input 'enrolment-code' inside a form with no method. This is safe today only because both forms mount after hydration. method='post', or no name attribute, would keep the code out of URLs if the card is ever server-rendered.
